messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High-rate CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS observed on serving-prod cluster node gpu-17. Container restarts and OOMs detected. Auto-evac triggered. Incident INC-2026-0317-17 created and assigned to ryan (oncall)
ryan (oncall): looking now. thanks. which services impacted?
leah (serving-runtime): seeing ~4 pods crashlooping on gpu-17 with 'CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS' in nsys logs. stack shows kernel-level pagewalk in nv_peer_access path. small repro attached in logs.
alex (sre): on it. can you paste the pod logs + kernel dmesg snippet? also confirm whether other nodes show similar traces.
leah (serving-runtime): paste: ```Container log: runtime: fatal error: cuda: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS at 0x7ffb...\nstack: inference_engine->kv_cache->nv_peer_access.c:142\n---\nKernel dmesg: [ 12345.678901] NVRM: GPU 0: watchdog timeout, aborting. [ 12345.678910] BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference````
ryan (oncall): ok cordoning node gpu-17 now to stop new pods scheduling. `kubectl cordon gpu-17`
joe (platform): nodenotify: cordon done. starting drain (grace 60s) `kubectl drain gpu-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`
alex (sre): repro looks like misaligned device address read from SMMU pagewalk -> illegal mem access. suspect driver/hardware interaction (possible kernel boundary-check regression). holding off kernel updates but need live mitigation.
maria (infra-eng): short-term mitigations: 1) reroute serving traffic off gpu-17 (done by cordon/drain) 2) scale up warm-capacity on GPU pool in us-east-1 to absorb load (in progress) 3) temporary model-variant fallback to quantized_CPU for those bursty routes.
sam (customer-success): hearing from 2 customers: latency spikes and ~1-2% error rate for large context chats. can we get an ETA for customer note?
ryan (oncall): assigning handoff to nate for overnight coverage. nate — full context above, node cordoned/draining, scaling + fallback active. Can you monitor and do hotfix attempts if needed?
nate (night-oncall): acknowledged. what hotfixes approved?
alex (sre): approved mitigations: revert recent driver micropatch applied to node pool (if present) and disable GPU peer-access on affected nodes via module param (non-disruptive toggle if kernel supports it). If revert fails, continue serving reroute and schedule node rebuilds. Avoid full kernel reboots during peak.
leah (serving-runtime): we already pushed routing rule to route model-id:tx-large to quantized_cpu variant for 15 minutes window: `redwood route update --model tx-large --fallback quantized_cpu --ttl 900`
maria (infra-eng): scaling event: +4 warm GPU pods requested (autoscaler triggered), expected to be ready in ~2m.
ryan (oncall): notify customers: sam can you prepare a short bulletin saying: brief description, affected regions (us-east-1), mitigation steps, expected impact (reduced throughput, elevated latencies), and we'll send once we confirm stable fallback in 10m?
sam (customer-success): drafting now. will post to customers once you give go.
joe (platform): quick check: `kubectl get pods -o wide -n serving | grep gpu-17` shows 3 evicted/crashloop pods, 1 running on alternate node.
leah (serving-runtime): adding stacktrace snippet (sanitized) to incident: ```inference_engine::serve_batch() at kv_cache.cpp:86\nread_device_mem(0x7f6b...): illegal aligned ptr (expected 8-byte alignment)\ncall trace: nv_peer_access_read -> smmu_pagewalk -> page_fault_handler```
alex (sre): confirmed similar but lower-frequency traces on gpu-9 and gpu-22 — could be same latent bug. recommend patch window and coordinated drain of nodes where driver micropatch present.
nate (night-oncall): will watch metrics and perform staged node rebuilds starting with gpu-17 after drain finishes. will attempt driver rollback on one repro node to validate.
deploy-bot: deployment rollback triggered for nodepool/gpu-micropatch -> creating new node template without micropatch
ryan (oncall): quick customer note: approved. sam, send now.
sam (customer-success): sent to affected customers: "We're investigating an infrastructure-level GPU memory error causing intermittent errors and elevated latency in us-east-1. Traffic is being rerouted; we expect degraded throughput for up to 1 hour while nodes are rebuilt. We'll update in 30m."
joe (platform): drain complete on gpu-17, node cordoned, rebuild queued.
maria (infra-eng): warm-capacity online, autoscaler added capacity. traffic back-filled to healthy nodes. error rate falling from 1.8% -> 0.4% in last 3m.
alex (sre): nate rolled back driver micropatch on test node (gpu-42) and repro stopped reproducing. plan: roll rollback across pool in controlled fashion. recommend marking incident as mitigated once rollouts pass smoke tests.
nate (night-oncall): rolling rollback in progress, will post progress summary in 15m.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: INC-2026-0317-17 status=mitigating assigned_to=nate priority=high
ryan (oncall): thanks team. handoff complete; I'll be available if escalation required.
sam (customer-success): will send update to customers in 30m with next status.
leah (serving-runtime): leaving logs + minimal repro in /incidents/INC-2026-0317-17/artifacts. please don't run repro on prod.
alex (sre): long-term actions: 1) kernel boundary-check audit for nv_peer_access codepath 2) add unit test covering misaligned address handling 3) improve crash detection to auto-fallback earlier. creating tickets after postmortem.
incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: INC-2026-0317-17 status=mitigated -> monitoring. last_update=6129991390
